terra.problem: The guess that Festus tidied up invents an action not given in the text.
The explanation is flat and repeats the distinction without Papa Dorin's warmth or humor.
Festus describes an opportunity to face one's accusers, not a guarantee that the accused will face them.
The explanation is generic and repeats the answer without Papa Dorin's voice.
The text does not say that jailers were not among those who made the case.
Festus describes an opportunity to defend oneself, not a requirement to stand up and speak.
The passage does not say Paul affirmed Jesus was alive while standing in front of the governor.
Saying Paul kept saying Jesus was alive adds repetition the passage does not state.
Calling Jesus being alive the whole argument leaves out Festus's mention of contentions about their religion.
Papa Dorin uses his mustache as hands; the joke gives him a hand.
The text does not establish that a report Festus owed had nothing to do with his request.
The explanation invents Festus's reason for telling Agrippa about Paul's custody.
The explanation is a plain sequence of facts without Papa Dorin's conversational voice.
Saying Agrippa gets a chance to hear Paul later gives away what happens beyond this passage. Here, Festus says Agrippa will hear him.
The explanation repeats the exchange without adding Papa Dorin's warmth or personality.
The text does not establish that nobody slipped in the back.
The passage describes pomp but does not say what Agrippa and Bernice wore. Plain clothes cannot be ruled out from that description.
Saying the line is meant to be heavy attributes an intention the text does not state.
The passage does not establish that there was no talk of a lighter punishment.
